items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: But I never had any problems with Dinah. She gave me complete freedom as to how to play behind her.

ctx.x: What was it like working with Joe?

With Joe it was great. I knew Joe from Chicago anyway, Joe lived, I think he grew up in Chicago, he was born in Georgia. And it was a good experience working with Joe. I had my trio working with Joe, which was Bob Cranshaw and Mickey Roker and myself. And we had a good time. We had the same manager, John Levy, and he thought it was a good idea to put the two together, to solve two things. We usually played a short set before Joe came on and then played for Joe. And that was a good experience. I really liked…
Nat told us some great stories about some of his compositions.

items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He has recorded and toured with Dizzy Gillespie, Dinah Washington and Joe Williams

ctx.x: Pianist Junior Mance was born in Chicago on October 10, 1928. He studied at Roosevelt College and gained early experience with Gene Ammons and Lester Young. During his military service, Junior played with the Adderley brothers, later joining their quintet in 1956. He has recorded and toured with Dizzy Gillespie, Dinah Washington and Joe Williams and currently leads his own trio.
The strong blues influence in his playing makes him immediately recognizable and he has composed a number of classic jazz tunes, including “Harlem Lullaby.”
